problem:
Let
$C=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$
and
$D=[\begin{aligned}7 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}].$
Then, the dimensions of $CD$ are{{field-1}}$\times $
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
We notice that $C$ is a $4\times 1$ matrix and $D$ is a $1\times 3$ matrix. 

There is $1$ column in $C$ and $1$ row in $D.$ Since the number of columns in $C$ equals the number of rows in $D,$ the matrices $C$ and $D$ are conformable for multiplication. 

The product $CD$ has dimensions $4\times 3:$

$$
{C}_{4\times \boxed{\text{1}}}{\times }_{✓}{D}_{\boxed{\text{1}}\times 3}={CD}_{4\times 3}
$$
